blogs.title: Beyond Type 1 and 2: Decoding the 'Young Diabetic' with a Three-Generation History
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic dilemma of distinguishing Monogenic Diabetes (MODY) from early-onset Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes. We analyze the specific clinical clues present in this case—including a strong three-generation family history, negative autoantibodies (GADA, IA-2), and preserved yet insufficient C-peptide—to build a framework for when to order genetic testing. The discussion includes the utility and limitations of MODY probability calculators in diverse populations and why relying solely on BMI or metabolic syndrome markers can lead to misdiagnosis.

blogs.title: The Glycosuria Trap: Why Renal Thresholds Matter in HNF1A-MODY Diagnosis
blogs.description: Focusing on the unique pathophysiology of HNF1A-MODY, this article explains how mutations in the HNF1A gene lead to reduced expression of SGLT2 transporters, causing glycosuria even at relatively modest blood glucose levels. We discuss how recognizing disproportionate glycosuria relative to hyperglycemia serves as a vital bedside clue for clinicians. Furthermore, we examine the dangerous implications of this mechanism regarding the use of SGLT2 inhibitors in these patients, highlighting risks like euglycemic DKA and severe dehydration.

blogs.title: From Insulin to GLP-1: Precision Medicine Strategies for HNF1A-MODY Management
blogs.description: While traditional teaching suggests sulfonylureas are first-line for HNF1A-MODY, this post analyzes the evolving landscape of treatment options illustrated by our case. We review the evidence supporting GLP-1 receptor agonists as a viable, potentially superior alternative for preserving beta-cell function and minimizing hypoglycemia risk compared to sulfonylureas or insulin. The narrative traces the patient's journey from an initial insulin/metformin regimen to a successful switch to dulaglutide and eventually oral maintenance, emphasizing how genetic confirmation drives therapeutic de-escalation.

blogs.title: Autonomic Dysfunction in Monogenic Diabetes: Unmasking Silent Neuropathy Early
blogs.description: This blog spotlights an often-overlooked feature of HNF1A-MODY: early-onset autonomic neuropathy. Using the case finding of severely reduced sudomotor function via electrochemical skin conductance testing (Sudoscan), we discuss how autonomic deficits can precede classic microvascular complications like retinopathy or nephropathy. The post argues for incorporating simple non-invasive autonomic screening tools into the workup of young diabetics suspected of having monogenic causes, offering insights into prognosis and quality-of-life management.

blogs.title: Novel Variants & ACMG Guidelines: Interpreting New Genetic Findings in Clinical Practice
blogs.description: Addressing the challenges of Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) results that reveal variants not listed in standard databases like ClinVar, this post breaks down how clinicians can interpret 'novel' mutations. Using the p.N270S variant found in this patient as a case study, we walk through the application of ACMG guidelines—considering segregation analysis, AlphaMissense scores, and functional domains—to classify variants as Likely Pathogenic. This serves as an educational guide for endocrinologists navigating complex genetic reports where database absence does not equal benign status.
